name: piping-toolset
description: Seven ASME B31.1 / B31.3 piping skills by pipingtoolset.com: pressure design, stress screening, CAESAR II / AutoPIPE load cases, PDF isometric to PCF, pipe support checks (AISC 360-22, ACI 318-19, ASCE 7-22), equipment nozzle loads (API 610 / 617 / 660 / 661 / 560 / 650, NEMA SM-23, PVP2011-57100) and bolted flanges (BPVC VIII-2 Part 4.16). A script computes every number; the skills embed no code tables. An optional connector serves cited ASME and API table values to signed-in paid accounts.

interface.longDescription:
PipingToolset is seven ASME B31.1 / B31.3 piping engineering skills from the people who build the free calculators at pipingtoolset.com, written and maintained by a practicing piping engineer at Flexible Piping Solutions LLC.

Skills: pressure-design (wall thickness, allowable pressure, branch reinforcement, bends, miters and leak-test pressure); stress-screening (sustained, occasional and expansion hand checks, the f factor by edition, which document supplies the SIFs, the formal-analysis exemption, support spans and spring variability); load-case-builder (complete static load case sets for CAESAR II and AutoPIPE with a QC gate); pipe-support (arm, column, welds, bolts, base plate, anchors and pier checked to ASCE 7-22, AISC 360-22, ACI 318-19 Chapter 17 and AWS D1.1, with ranked code-passing alternatives and a calc report); iso-to-pcf (PDF stress isometrics to a validated CAESAR II PCF); nozzle-load (API 610, API 617 / 611 / 612, NEMA SM-23, API 660 / 661 / 560, API 650 Annex P and the PVP2011-57100 method for vessels with no vendor allowable); bolted-flange (a pressure-equivalent screen, then the BPVC Section VIII Division 2 Part 4.16 analysis).

Three rules hold in every skill. The assistant never does the arithmetic: every number comes from a bundled standard-library Python script run on the inputs you supplied. The assistant never recalls a code table value: allowable stresses, SIFs, spans, flange ratings and gasket factors come from your own copy of the standard, or from the optional connector below with its citation, and a request for just the number with neither is declined with the table, row and edition named instead. The edition is an input, never a silent default: anything you leave unanswered is marked ASSUMED on the calc sheet.

Optional Engineering Data connector. A remote MCP server, pipingtoolset-data, at https://pipingtoolset.com/mcp, declared for Claude Code and Cowork and added by hand in Codex and ChatGPT. Every skill works without it, and the skills and their scripts make no network calls. When the connector is enabled, the assistant sends only what is needed to find one row (the standard, material, temperature or size), never your full inputs, loads or project data. With no account it serves worked examples of the data-free modules, SKEY and PCF mappings, AISC shapes and pointers to where a value is printed. With a signed-in paid pipingtoolset.com account it serves ASME and API code-table values at the level of your plan, each cited to standard, edition, table and row. Currently, Pro covers B31.3 Table A-1C and B31.1 Appendix A allowable stresses and bolting, the B31.3 E, W and Y and B31.1 E and y factor tables, B31J Table 1-1 component rows (row text only; the SIF stays yours to supply), B31.1 Table 121.5-1 spans, BPE tables and B36.10M / B36.19M dimensions. Pro Plus adds B16.5 ratings and dimensions, B16.20, UCS-66 and VIII-2 Table 4.16.1 gasket factors. Ultimate currently adds API 610 Tables 5a and 5b, API 560 Tables 7 to 10, API 660 Table 2 and API 661 Table 4. PVP2011-57100 tables, ASCE 7-22, AISC 360, ACI and NEMA SM-23 currently return a pointer (table, row, column and edition) and no value. Sign-in goes through pipingtoolset.com and requires you to confirm that your assistant account is set not to train on your conversations. A served value is still verified against your own copy before issue. Setup for each host: https://pipingtoolset.com/docs/connector/

Intended for piping stress and mechanical engineers who need results they can reproduce and defend. Requires a host that can run Python 3.9 or newer; in a host that cannot run scripts the skill stops at the interview and says so. Results are engineering aids; the engineer of record verifies them before issue. The plugin carries no telemetry and needs no account, and without the connector nothing you enter reaches PipingToolset or Flexible Piping Solutions. Open source under the Apache License 2.0; source and releases are on GitHub.
capabilities: Runs bundled Python 3.9+ scripts locally; the scripts make no network calls
Optional remote connector: cited code-table lookups, sign-in at pipingtoolset.com for paid plans
